source_review.notes: Checked six official/primary sources. DynamoDB documentation supports surface-specific eventual/strong reads and committed-read behavior. Spanner documentation supports strong reads, snapshots, serializability, and external consistency distinctions. Azure Cosmos DB supports strong, bounded-staleness, session, consistent-prefix, and eventual levels plus token/session scope and request overrides. RFC 9110 supports authoritative ETags on created representations and conditional requests. Provider-specific guarantees are attributed and not generalized beyond documented surfaces.

evidence: Checked write/read versions v_w/v_r, high-water h, epoch e, checkpoint c_p, time-to-visible L_s/T_s, deadline B, catch-up/execution/reserve W_c/W_e/R, and RPO for consistent scopes/units.
Confirmed version comparisons require the same resource/order/epoch.
Confirmed durability RPO remains distinct from read visibility lag.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Opaque provider/session tokens need not expose a client-comparable scalar.

evidence: Confirmed version floor rejects replica 40 when required write/high-water is 42 and rejects 11 after observing 12.
Recomputed 300+40+30=370 ms greater than 250 ms in the projection-wait example.
Recomputed 180+35+25=240 ms greater than 220 ms and leader 80+35+25=140 ms within 220 ms in the exercise.
Checked restore/failover examples 70>68 and exact ten examples/five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Lag and route estimates are scenarios; production decisions require conservative tail estimates and admission.

evidence: Derived monotonic observation from high-water update by maximum and read admission v_r>=h.
Constructed source-at-42/index-at-40 counterexample proving storage consistency does not transfer to a derived view.
Confirmed W_c+W_e+R>=B makes wait infeasible under the stated estimates.
Constructed failover state below required token proving read routing cannot manufacture missing durability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Arguments explicitly require complete token propagation, comparable versions, and accurate authority/epoch.

evidence: Reviewed read-your-writes, monotonic reads/writes, writes-follow-reads, eventual/bounded/session/linearizable/serializable/external/snapshot guarantees and concurrent supersession.
Reviewed resource/list/search/count/cache/projection/analytics surfaces, create/update/delete, overlays, filters/sorts/pages, multi-resource snapshots, and conditional writes.
Reviewed one/many partitions, vector/token growth, scope/epoch mismatch, forgery/future tokens, client/session/device loss, affinity, autoscaling, and authorization separation.

Reviewed replica/index/cache lag, event loss/reorder, leader change, partition, regional failover/failback, weak durability/RPO, backup restore, reshard, continuous writes, overload, and deadline expiry.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans semantics, surfaces, concurrency, tokens, security, topology, durability, and recovery.

evidence: Confirmed write acknowledgement states accepted/committed/replicated/projected milestones explicitly.
Confirmed every qualifying read enforces its scoped high-water or fails/degrades explicitly.
Confirmed tokens cannot grant authorization and malformed/high/mismatched tokens cannot force unbounded waits.
Confirmed caches and projections prove a checkpoint/version before satisfying a floor.
Confirmed retries preserve effect identity and failover never silently resets consistency or epoch.
invariant_checking.notes: Session consistency is never described as global latest or global durability.

evidence: Reviewed session-floor proof and confirmed it is scoped to comparable versions and complete token propagation.
Reviewed cross-surface counterexample and confirmed barrier/overlay/weaker contract are required.
Reviewed deadline feasibility and confirmed alternate eligible source/pending/failure paths remain.
Reviewed durability counterexample and confirmed consistency controls cannot repair unreplicated state.
proof_review.notes: No database consistency label is claimed to automatically cover caches or asynchronous indexes.

evidence: Confirmed four arguments are labeled with assumptions/counterexamples.
Confirmed AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and IETF behaviors are attributed to their documented scopes.
Confirmed example lag, versions, deadlines, and routing costs are scenarios rather than standards.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Formal session properties, provider product semantics, API policy, and empirical visibility SLOs are distinct.

evidence: All six official/primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All versions, checkpoints, lags, deadlines, route costs, epochs, and RPO examples are labeled scenarios.

Actual consistency support per surface, lag tails, token behavior, escalation capacity, cache/index checkpoints, failover durability, snapshot retention, and violation rates remain explicit integration/history/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production database, projection, region topology, client fleet, or consistency history was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed guarantee names, acknowledgement milestones, read surfaces, authoritative versions, session high-water, read enforcement, caches/projections, pagination/snapshots, failover, concurrent writers, optimistic UI, deadlines, observability, and history testing as one API visibility contract.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through visibility matrices, returned versions/ETags, scoped opaque session tokens, bounded wait/leader escalation, versioned caches, projection barriers/overlays, snapshot cursors, epoch-safe failover, If-Match writes, direct violation telemetry, and generated histories.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module moves from consistency vocabulary through write/read contracts and session enforcement, then caches/projections, snapshots/topology, concurrency, deadlines, observation, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
